This term means 'king'. It evokes authority, sovereignty, and power. 1.epoque: Psalm 145 was written during the reign of David, a period when Israel was unified and prosperous under his leadership. David, as king, had a profound understanding of God's sovereignty in his life and in the kingdom.

1.commentaire: This psalm teaches us the importance of worship in our daily lives. By proclaiming God as our king, we affirm our commitment to live according to His precepts. May our praise be a natural response to His goodness and greatness, encouraging us to bless His name at every moment.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to bless' and evokes the idea of giving thanks, praising, or honoring. Its root is related to the idea of granting prosperity and divine favor. It pushes us to see His hand in all our circumstances and to live in recognition of His eternal goodness.

mots.sens: This term means 'good', 'pleasant', or 'beneficial'. It evokes divine goodness, an essential quality of God that manifests in His actions toward humanity. In the context of this verse, God's goodness is immense, highlighting His generosity and infinite kindness toward His creation.

By celebrating His justice, we are encouraged to imitate His ways and seek righteousness in our actions. May our lives reflect this immense goodness, and may our words and deeds glorify God.

This term means 'to listen' or 'to hear.' In the context of invocation, it emphasizes the idea that God is attentive to the prayers and supplications of His people. This reinforces the notion that sincere invocation is heard by God, encouraging believers to turn to Him in their needs.

This word means 'in truth' or 'with sincerity.' It implies authenticity in invocation, emphasizing that God responds to those who come to Him with a pure and honest heart. This underscores the importance of spiritual integrity in our relationship with God.

18.epoque: This psalm was composed in an ancient context, probably during the monarchy of Israel, where prayer and invocation of God were essential practices in the spiritual life of the Hebrew people.
18.passage: Psalm 145 is a hymn of praise that celebrates God's greatness and His goodness toward all. This verse highlights the promise of God's closeness to those who sincerely invoke Him, reinforcing the idea that prayer is a means of establishing a personal relationship with Him.
18.culture: In Hebrew culture, invoking God was often associated with rituals and communal prayers. Sincerity in prayer was essential, as it reflected the faithfulness and devotion of the believer toward God.
18.interpretation: This verse reminds us that God is always accessible to those who seek His presence with a sincere heart. Invocation is not merely a recitation of words, but an act of faith that establishes a deep connection with the Creator.
18.commentaire: This psalm encourages us to approach God with confidence, knowing that He is close to us when we sincerely invoke Him. In our moments of distress or joy, we can find comfort and support in Him. Let us cultivate a life of authentic prayer, for it is in this intimacy that we discover the depth of His love and faithfulness.

mots.sens: This word means 'to desire' or 'to take pleasure in.' It evokes a deep and sincere longing, often associated with divine will. In this verse, it emphasizes that God takes pleasure in granting the desires of those who fear Him, thus revealing God's benevolent and attentive nature towards His faithful.

This term means 'to hear' or 'to listen.' It implies not only hearing but also active attention and response to what is heard. In the context of this verse, it underscores that God is attentive to the cries of those who honor Him, and that He responds to their calls with compassion.

This word means 'to save' or 'to deliver.' It is often used in the context of divine deliverance. In this verse, it highlights God's commitment to saving those who fear Him, affirming His faithfulness and power to intervene in the lives of His servants.

This term means 'to fear' or 'to respect.' It implies an attitude of reverence and submission towards God. In this verse, the fact that God grants the desires of those who fear Him shows that the fear of God is the foundation of an authentic relationship with Him, marked by trust and obedience.

19.epoque: Psalm 145 is attributed to David, a king of Israel who lived around 1000 B.C. This psalm is set in a context where the people of Israel seek to understand the nature of God and His interaction with humanity.
19.passage: This psalm is a hymn of praise that celebrates the greatness of God and His goodness towards all. Verse 19 highlights the intimate relationship between God and those who fear Him, emphasizing His commitment to meet their needs.
19.culture: In Hebrew culture, the fear of God is a fundamental value, representing a respectful and loving relationship with the Creator. It also implies trust in His providence and His ability to intervene in difficult situations.
19.interpretation: This verse reveals that God is attentive to the desires of those who fear Him and that He responds to their cries. It underscores the importance of the fear of God in the lives of believers, which is the foundation of a relationship of trust and dependence on Him.
19.commentaire: This psalm reminds us that God is close to those who honor Him and that He is attentive to their needs. As believers, we are called to live in the fear of God, trusting Him to fulfill our desires according to His will. This encourages us to pray with assurance, knowing that our God is a God who hears and saves.

mots.sens: This term designates one who loves, who has a deep and sincere affection. It comes from the root 'אהב' (aheb), which implies attachment and devotion. In the context of this verse, love for the Lord is associated with an intimate and protective relationship, emphasizing that those who love God are under His benevolent care.

This verb means to keep, protect, or watch over. It evokes the idea of active vigilance and divine protection. In this verse, it emphasizes that the Lord takes care of those who love Him, preserving them from dangers and harmful influences, which reflects God's faithfulness to His people.

This word designates the wicked, one who acts unjustly or immorally. It is often used in the Psalms to describe those who oppose God's will. In this verse, the destruction of the wicked is an affirmation of divine justice, indicating that God does not leave injustice unpunished.

20.epoque: This psalm was written at a time when the people of Israel faced adversities and injustices, often beset by powerful enemies. David, as king, expresses here confidence in divine justice and protection.
20.passage: Psalm 145 is a hymn of praise that celebrates the greatness and goodness of God. In this context, verse 20 emphasizes the promise of protection for those who love God, while affirming judgment on the wicked.
20.culture: In Hebrew culture, love for God is central and is manifested through obedience to His commandments. The notion of divine justice is also paramount, where reward and punishment are recurring themes in biblical writings.
20.interpretation: This verse reminds us that love for God is reciprocal; those who commit to Him benefit from His protection. At the same time, it highlights the reality of divine judgment on those who choose to live in evil.
20.commentaire: The Lord promises to keep those who love Him, which encourages us to cultivate our relationship with Him. As believers, we must remember that our love for God is the key to our spiritual security. This verse urges us to remain faithful and to trust in God's justice, knowing that He watches over us and is our refuge in difficult times.

mots.sens: This word means 'praise' and is derived from the root 'הָלַל' (halal), which evokes the idea of celebrating or giving glory. In the context of this verse, it underscores the importance of proclaiming the wonders of God, and it is often associated with a joyful and public expression of gratitude towards the Lord. Theologically, this reminds us that praise is a natural response to the greatness of God and should be a continuous practice in the lives of believers.

This term means 'blessed' and is related to the idea of receiving divine favor. In the context of this verse, 'to bless' implies not only an act of gratitude but also a recognition of God's holiness and sovereignty. Spiritually, this invites us to understand that blessing the name of God is an act of worship that should be perpetual and universal, encompassing all of creation.

This word means 'name' and holds deep significance in Hebrew culture, where a name is often associated with a person's identity and reputation. In this verse, God's name is considered holy and worthy of praise, which underscores the importance of recognizing who He is in our worship. Theologically, this reminds us that the name of God represents His character and authority, and that we must honor Him in all our expressions of praise.

21.epoque: Psalm 145 is attributed to David, a king of Israel who lived around the 10th century B.C., a time marked by political struggles and deep spiritual aspirations.
21.passage: This psalm is part of the acrostics and is a hymn of praise, highlighting the greatness of God and His wonderful works. The entire chapter is an exhortation to celebrate God's goodness and mercy towards all His creation.
21.culture: In Hebrew culture, praise was an integral part of communal and religious life, often expressed through songs, prayers, and rituals. The psalms were used in public worship, reinforcing collective identity and relationship with God.
21.interpretation: This verse calls us to active and continuous praise towards God, emphasizing that every human being has a role to play in glorifying His name. The mention of 'all flesh' indicates that praise is not reserved for a specific group, but is a universal call to recognize the holiness of God.
21.commentaire: This psalm reminds us that praise should be at the heart of our daily lives. By proclaiming God's goodness and blessing His name, we participate in a divine work that transcends time and space. May our mouths always be filled with praise, not only in words but also in actions, thus reflecting the greatness of our God in the world.
